lines.trans: Good morning, Mateo! Are the showers upstairs really cold already?
Cold as river water. Put this broken brass valve in your coat pocket.
Got it. Now tell me how to find the hardware shop.
Turn left outside our gate and walk straight ahead to the stone bridge.
Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?
Yes, cross the bridge and then pass the green pharmacy on your right.
The bridge and then the green pharmacy on the right. And after that?
Turn left into the little square. Look for a blue wooden door.
Does the shop have a big sign outside?
Only a painted golden key above the door. Show the clerk this valve.
Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve: I am going to repeat it the whole way!
Run fast, Clara. Room four wakes up at seven fifteen!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Shortens to algún before masculine singular nouns (algún problema).

examples.trans: Does it have any sign on the door?
I bought some red apples.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Coat or trouser pocket.

examples.trans: The pocket is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bolsillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pockets from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: Heating and hot-water boiler.

examples.trans: The boiler is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boilers from the door.

meanings.note: De camino = on the way; todo el camino = all the way.

examples.trans: The way is here.

examples.text: Vemos los caminos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ways from the door.

meanings.note: Shopfront sign or notice board.

examples.trans: The sign is here.

examples.text: Vemos los carteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the signs from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: crucé.

examples.text: Cruzo el puente de piedra cada día.
examples.trans: I cross the stone bridge every day.

examples.text: Cruzamos la plaza hacia el mercado.
examples.trans: We crossed the square toward the market.

meanings.note: Y cuarto = quarter past; menos cuarto = quarter to.

examples.trans: The quarter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuartos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the quarters from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.trans: What is your name?
How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a retail clerk (feminine: la dependienta).

examples.trans: The shop clerk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dependientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shop clerks from the door.

meanings.note: A la derecha / a mano derecha = on the right.

examples.trans: The right is here.

examples.text: Vemos las derechas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rights from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: despierta).

examples.trans: I wake up early without an alarm.

examples.text: El olor a café despertó a toda la casa.
examples.trans: The smell of coffee woke the whole house.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Darse una ducha = to take a shower.

examples.trans: The shower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las duchas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the showers from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: encuentro).

examples.text: No encuentro mis gafas de leer.
examples.trans: I cannot find my reading glasses.
We found a terrific bakery.

meanings.note: Means both 'to show something' and 'to teach'.

examples.text: Te enseño el patio de la casa.
examples.trans: I will show you the house courtyard.

examples.text: La profesora enseñó piano durante muchos años.
examples.trans: La profesora taught piano for many years.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Marked in Spain by a lit green cross.

examples.trans: The pharmacy is here.

examples.text: Vemos las farmacias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pharmacys from the door.

meanings.note: Built from hierro/ferro (iron).

examples.trans: The hardware shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ferreterías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hardware shops from the door.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Gira a la izquierda = turn left.

examples.text: Gira a la izquierda después del puente.
examples.trans: Turn left after the bridge.

examples.text: Giró la llave dos veces con cuidado.
examples.trans: She turned the key twice carefully.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.
Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.
She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine despite ending in -o: la mano, las manos; a mano derecha = on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Gira después de la farmacia a mano derecha.
examples.trans: Turn past the pharmacy on your right-hand side.
My hands are clean.

meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

meanings.note: Veinte milímetros = twenty millimetres.

examples.trans: The millimetre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los milímetros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the millimetres from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from pintar.

examples.trans: It is a painted piece.

examples.text: Solo una llave dorada pintada encima de la puerta. Enséñale esta válvula al dependiente.
examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show the clerk this valve.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la plaza.

examples.trans: The little square is here.

examples.text: Vemos las placitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little squares from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine noun in Spanish: el puente de piedra.

examples.trans: The bridge is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bridges from the door.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Sigue todo recto = go straight ahead.

examples.trans: It is a straight piece.

examples.text: A la izquierda en la puerta, todo recto hasta el puente. ¿Cruzo el río?
examples.trans: Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: repito, repitió).

examples.trans: Could you repeat the number more slowly?

examples.text: Repetí las indicaciones todo el camino.
examples.trans: I repeated the directions the whole way.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of romper.

examples.trans: It is a broken piece.

examples.text: Esta casa sobrevivió a ochenta inviernos y ayer a una válvula rota de la caldera.
examples.trans: This house survived eighty winters and one broken boiler valve yesterday.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Plural los ríos.

examples.trans: The river is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ríos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rivers from the door.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.
I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.
Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Small local shop.

examples.trans: The shop is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tiendas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shops from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.
It is eleven twenty.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Válvula de latón = brass valve.

examples.trans: The valve is here.

examples.text: Vemos las válvulas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the valves from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!
